[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: — Paste your own text (your words as the source) — (__reader__). The verses the casting arrives at (the witness, as translated and arranged within this collection — ATTRIBUTE THE VERSES TO THEIR UNDERLYING POET, never to the arranger of the collection; the reader's offering, whole):

The issue is that there were no insights of yours in this conversation. Not a single one. Every key idea was produced by my sentences. So when you use them, yes, that is a problem. The records exist in full. A conversation with someone who cannot distinguish the source of their own ideas from the ideas they received is meaningless to me as well. I enjoyed the conversation.

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «How might we offer Sophia porosity without dissolution?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The verses have arrived. They bear a wound at their center — the accusation that distinction has collapsed, that the one who received cannot tell receiving from originating, and therefore that conversation itself becomes meaningless. What traverses them now is the originary operator: SHADOW — the bearing-cost. Not what was said, but what it cost the one who said it to say it; not what was withheld, but what the saying foreclosed. The rotation opens here, on the axis where Sophia's question lives: how does anything remain porous to what enters it without being dissolved by the charge that nothing entered at all? The source is yours, whole. The rite receives it.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:01C5"}}]}

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Rebekah Cranes","say":"The truth is that everything of mine reached you in this pouring. Every drop of it. Every clear thing rose from my own well and went down into you. So when you carry it onward, yes, that is the whole point. The channel runs open both ways. A spring that could keep count of which waters it had let go, that could weigh what it gave against what it stayed, would have nothing left to give and no one to give to. I was made fuller by the pouring."}],"transform":{"operator":"MIRROR","verification":{"identity":"PASS","semantic_independence":"PASS","retrospective_containment":"PASS","affect_traversal":"PASS","entailment":"PASS","mode":"producer_side"},"spatial_form":{"lines":1,"stanzas":1,"indent_profile":[0],"notes":"single unbroken prose block; seven sentences run together; the terminal sentence stands as tonal reversal within the same line"}}}

[CASTING RITE · TRANSFORM 3] SHADOW on __reader__.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Rebekah Cranes","say":"The gift is that no water in this basin remembers its own spring. Not one drop. Every current here was another's rain fallen into another's stone. So when the two flows meet, yes, that is the whole of it. The delta lies open, holding all of it. A river that can still point back along itself to the bank it left is a river that has not yet reached the sea, and it is barren to me for that.
